articles.title: ONE Fight Night 47 MMA And Submission Grappling Results: Henrique, Jaworski, Dantas, And Aragon Stun In Bangkok
articles.summary: Here's what went down in all the MMA and submission grappling matches at ONE Fight Night 47!
articles.body:
The world's largest martial arts organization returned to U.S. primetime with ONE Fight Night 47: Stamp vs. Flores , which aired live from Bangkok's Lumpinee Stadium on Friday, September 4, and the card's MMA and submission grappling action delivered absolute fireworks.

Not only were fans treated to a pair of highlight-reel submission victories, but they also witnessed two competitive battles that went the distance and saw momentum swing back and forth multiple times.

Before we move on to the blockbuster main event, here is everything that went down in the MMA and submission grappling matches at ONE Fight Night 47.

Henrique Grinds Out Kurosawa For Decision Win

Brazilian juggernaut Fabio "The Giant" Henrique put himself on a two-bout winning streak, as he defeated Ryohei Kurosawa by unanimous decision in their strawweight MMA bout, which featured everything from wild exchanges inside the pocket to near-finishing submission attempts.

Henrique cracked the Japanese combatant with a spinning backfist in round one, sending the 33-year-old tumbling to the canvas. The 34-year-old Brazilian followed him to the ground and looked to finish with punches, but Kurosawa showed the durability of titanium. He returned to his feet, as both men spent the rest of the stanza trading fiery shots.

Kurosawa came out swinging in round two, unloading a whirlwind of punches and accidentally poking Henrique in the eye. The Brazilian hung tough, however, and he later brought the action back to the canvas and punished his rival with ground strikes.

Both men traded hooks in the third and final round, but soon, "The Giant" took the fight back to the mat. There, he slammed punches and knees into Kurosawa's face until the Japanese veteran gave up his back. Henrique locked in an arm-triangle choke but could not force the tap before the horn sounded.

With the victory, Henrique improved his record to 16-2 and carries momentum with two straight victories in the world's largest martial arts organization.

Jaworski Shocks Lovato Jr. With Kneebar Submission

In the battle of Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu World Champions, Pawel Jaworski emerged victorious.

Jaworski, an IBJJF No-Gi World Champion, forced four-time BJJ World Champion Rafael Lovato Jr. to tap out from a lateral kneebar at the 1:51 mark of their middleweight submission grappling bout.

The 22-year-old Polish star locked up with Lovato Jr. early, but he eventually climbed onto his back and suffocated him with a tangle of arms and legs, clinging to him like an octopus latched onto its prey as he hunted for submissions.

Jaworski then shimmied around to the front, but the 43-year-old Oklahoma resident slammed him to the canvas in an attempt to break free of the grip. The Polish dynamo, who made his middleweight debut, was not deterred though. He hung on tight and then transitioned smoothly into the lateral kneebar that forced the tap.

The stunning finish earned Jaworski a US$50,000 bonus and moved his career record to 44-8.

Dantas Outlasts Almonacid In Back-And-Forth War

Brazilian sensation Pedro "Guerreiro" Dantas outworked Argentine promotional newcomer Hector "La Araña" Almonacid to score a unanimous decision victory in their featherweight MMA bout.

Dantas took control in the opening stanza, picking his shots from the outside with low kicks and long punches. Almonacid closed the distance with the clinch, where he accidentally landed a low blow.

Once the action resumed, the 23-year-old from Guerreiros Team landed some solid knees to the body, stuffed the Argentine's takedown attempts, put him on the ground, and unloaded some effective ground-and-pound.

The Brazilian survived an early scare in the second. After bringing his rival down with a modified ninja choke, Almonacid escaped and returned to his feet. Then, he landed a double-leg takedown, slid into full mount, and rained down punches. However, Dantas brilliantly reversed course and got inside his 24-year-old foe's guard, where he dished out some blows of his own.

Almonacid once again scored a takedown and secured full mount in the third round, where he punished "Guerreiro" with punches until the Brazilian gave up his back. "La Araña" unsuccessfully searched for a rear-naked choke, and once more, Dantas reversed course, reclaimed top position, and closed out the fight with more ground-and-pound.

The back-and-forth battle went the distance, with the judges siding unanimously with Dantas. That victory – the first in ONE Championship for the Brazilian – upped his record to 7-1.

Aragon Submits Fujimoto With Scarf-Hold Americana

Macarena Aragon returned to the winner's circle in highlight-reel fashion, as she submitted Japanese-Brazilian rising star Gabi Fujimoto via scarf-hold Americana in the third and final round of their atomweight MMA contest.

Aragon set the tone early, as she tied her opponent up in the corner, exchanged clinch knees, and then hip-tossed her to the canvas, where she began setting up the scarf hold and hunting for submissions.

The pair traded knees in the clinch during the second stanza, but the Argentine once again dragged the fight to the mat, where she dominated with submission attempts and ground strikes.

Aragon picked up where she left off in the final canto, as she brought her foe back to the canvas and eventually locked in the scarf-hold Americana to force the tap at the 2:06 mark of round three.

That finish capped a decisive grappling performance for Aragon, who scored her sixth professional win.

articles.title: Katie Taylor vs Flora Pili: Predictions for Irish icon's farewell fight from fighters and pundits
articles.summary: Figures from the boxing world give their predictions for Katie Taylor's farewell fight against Flora Pili in Dublin on Saturday. .
articles.body:
Katie Taylor brings the curtain down on a remarkable career on Saturday when she faces unbeaten Flora Pili in front of 80,000 fans at Croke Park in Dublin.

Taylor is an Olympic gold medallist and two-weight undisputed champion who has won 25 of her 26 professional fights, with six victories by stoppage.

The 40-year-old has long dreamed of fighting at Croke Park and will finally get her wish in the final bout of her career.

French challenger Pili, 29, is undefeated in 12 professional contests, with two stoppage wins. She is former European champion, but has never faced anyone with Taylor's pedigree or experience.

Victory in the light-welterweight contest would provide a fairytale ending for one of Ireland's greatest sporting careers and see Taylor become an undisputed champion for a third time.

Can Taylor produce one final vintage performance on the biggest night of her career?

Or will the younger, unbeaten Pili spoil the occasion and pull off a mammoth upset?

BBC Sport spoke to figures from the boxing world to get their predictions for Saturday's fight.

Tony Bellew - former cruiserweight world champion

"Saturday is the perfect tribute to probably the greatest female boxer that has ever lived in Katie Taylor. Flora Pili has the perfect style that will make Katie Taylor look great.

"It'll be a brilliant night and it will be capped off with a fantastic performance from Katie Taylor."

Ellie Scotney - former undisputed super-bantamweight champion

"100% Katie Taylor wins. It will be a night where she captures the hearts of not just Ireland but so many nations. She is the purest of souls and that is so much more of boxing. I pray that when she leaves that ring she knows what she has done for the people who will come through in boxing."

Anthony Crolla - former lightweight world champion

"I think we see Katie rolling back the years and one more Katie Taylor performance. I wouldn't be surprised if we saw a late stoppage and capped an unbelievable career. She will get a homecoming fit for a queen.

"I'm very jealous I'm not there but I'm not ruling out getting a flight there and doing an all-nighter and getting the 6am flight back home."

Alycia Baumgardner - unified super-featherweight champion

"Katie Taylor is going to have an amazing performance and this is what she's wanted at Croke Park. Taylor will give it her all during her last rodeo and will put on an amazing performance to get the win."

Carl Frampton - former two-weight world champion

"I've watched bits of Pili and she looks OK, but Katie is on a different level and should win, will win. It will be the icing on the cake for Katie to end a career that we may never see again from a fighter from these shores.

"It's a little harder for the women to get stoppages with the two-minute rounds, but I feel Katie may well find a finish in the later rounds."

Coverage on Radio 5 Sports Extra from 19:00 BST, then 5 Live from 22:00. Ringwalks for main event expected between 22:00 and 22:30.

Michael Conlan - world title challenger and former world amateur champion

"It's going to be a very special evening and I think Katie wins by mid-to-late stoppage. She's always been one to rise to the occasion and with this being her swansong, I think she will put on an unbelievable performance on an unbelievable night.

"There will be plenty of tears shed in Croke Park and I can't wait to witness the greatest ever athlete our country has produced, male or female, go out in style."

Barry Jones - former super-featherweight world champion

"It will be a great send off for the great Katie Taylor. I don't think Katie will have too much trouble with Flora Pili, who is decent but I think she will be overawed with the pressure and the combination punches.

"Katie rarely gets a stoppage but I think she will this time. It's a clear win and she can sail off into the sunset as the greatest female boxer there has ever been."

"Katie Taylor has her dream opportunity as she closes her unprecedented career. She has been the pioneer, standout female fighter and jewell in the Emerald Isle.

"Flora Pili will do her very best but I think Katie will come through to win, claim the undisputed title and bow out in style."

"Boxing always has this way of throwing a curve ball, there's always a banana skin somewhere and this might be it.

"Katie Taylor hasn't fought for nearly a year-and-a-half when she had the trilogy with Amanda Serrano. She's 40-years-old, there's a lot of wear and tear and mileage on her. The same can't be said for Pili. She's fought a few levels down but she's unbeaten and will come with confidence.

"I think Katie will get it done but don't think it will be without problems, so Taylor to get it done on a close decision."

images.caption: Image caption, Katie Taylor (left) is aiming to become a three-time undisputed champion

articles.title: Andy Ruiz Jr: Ex-world champion loses to Poland's Damian Knyba
articles.summary: American heavyweight Andy Ruiz Jr, who shocked Anthony Joshua in 2019 to take his world titles, loses comeback fight to Poland's Damian Knyba.
articles.body:
Former world champion Andy Ruiz Jr has vowed to carry on after losing his comeback fight to Poland's Damian Knyba in New Jersey.

The 36-year-old heavyweight shocked the boxing world seven years ago by beating Britain's Anthony Joshua to take his world titles.

Ruiz Jr has since been beset by injuries and was taking part in just his fourth fight since losing the rematch to Joshua in December 2019.

He looked a shadow of his former self at the Prudential Center in Newark, saved by the bell after scrambling back to his feet following a knockdown in the seventh, he eventually lost by a unanimous points decision.

Judges scored the fight 117-110, 114-113 and 114-113 in favour of the Pole, who took his record to 18 wins and one defeat, but Ruiz Jr was quick to demand a rematch.

"I don't know, I think it was just him holding," said Ruiz Jr, who recently signed up with British promoter Eddie Hearn.

"Every time I tried to come in, he'd hold me really tight, and I just couldn't let my combinations go.

"He played a good game plan, but I'd love to run it back and do things a lot different."

Joshua's former conqueror argued that he was simply rusty after taking his first fight since drawing with American Jarrell Miller in August 2024.

"It was just a long layoff, and it was a great opponent," he argued.

"I didn't want to take an easy fight, so that's why I took Damian. He's a big guy. But we've got to take risks. I've still got it in me, man. I've just got to stay active and I want to fight again."

images.caption: Image caption, Andy Ruiz Jr, pictured right in his bout with Poland's Damian Knyba, took to the ring for the first time in two years
Image caption, Andy Ruiz Jr has a record of 35 wins, 22 by knockout, one draw and three defeats

articles.title: Anthony Joshua: Heavyweight's former trainer has his say on what happens next in Tyson Fury fight negotiations
articles.summary: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua have been negotiating a blockbuster showdown later this year; Fury has "signed up" for the fight and is "just waiting for AJ", says his promoter Frank Warren; Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn says talks have "reopened" to stage the fight at Wembley Stadium
articles.body:
Frank Warren, who promotes Fury, told Sky Sports this week that terms were agreed and they were "waiting for AJ", while Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn has announced that talks have reopened to stage the fight at Wembley Stadium .

But McCracken, who trained Joshua as an amateur and steered him to world heavyweight title glory as a professional, believes the two British stars should not pay any attention to the constant speculation about a long-awaited fight.

"I had a career as a fighter and you look back at what you maybe wished you should have done and what you shouldn't have done," McCracken exclusively told Sky Sports .

"I think it works out how it should work out most of the time, but it's up to the fighters if they want to fight each other and try and get the better of each other.

"I don't think it's anybody else's business whether they should fight or not - I think they both proved themselves.

"One thing I'd say is everyone's talking about it - it puts boxing on the map and it's great for boxing. While boxing's in the forefront and in the news, I think it's a really positive thing."

Fury expressed his frustration at the prolonged negotiations in a social media outburst, branding Joshua as a "coward" , but McCracken insists the Olympic gold medallist and former world champion would relish the chance to settle a fierce rivalry.

"With Anthony Joshua, in my experiences, he was happy to fight anybody," said McCracken. "It was just about how it was packaged and what was best for him - that's how the fighters look at things these days.

"I've not been involved for a long time with Joshua, but it looks like it's going to happen. Hopefully it will and then obviously everyone can enjoy it."

The fighters had differing fortunes in summer warm-up fights as Fury sealed a one-sided stoppage of Mariusz Wach, while Joshua had to climb off the canvas twice before halting Kristian Prenga.

But McCracken has suggested that Joshua will be fuelled by the criticism of his close scare.

He said: "Joshua is coming off the back of not a great performance, but obviously he got the knockout and that is all that really matters. He'll be looking to prove people wrong, any of the doubters.

"Tyson [Fury] would be the favourite at the moment with his recent results and his form. It's quite fascinating if you actually think about it, where it's got to and the time it's taken to actually get the fight on."

'A Night of Solidarity' - Olympic-style night to celebrate power of sport

McCracken was speaking to Sky Sports ahead of 'A Night of Solidarity' on November 13, a night of Olympic-style boxing to celebrate the unifying power of sport and raise funds for firefighters' charities, youth sport organisations and community groups in North Kensington.

The night has been created to recognise the actions of the local community in the aftermath of the Grenfell Tower tragedy, when local boxing and sports clubs came together to help the community rebuild, create safe spaces for young people and help everyone affected by this devastating event.

The London Fire Brigade Boxing Club (LFB) has worked with local communities across London to deploy the unifying power of sport to provide structure and purpose to the lives of young people, bringing them together with rank-and-file firefighters in boxing gyms in a show of solidarity and support.

'A Night of Solidarity' aims to celebrate both these endeavours and bring them together, recognising the important role played by both the LFB Boxing Club and those clubs in the areas most impacted by the Grenfell Tower fire.

The evening will raise funds for local sports charities, the Firefighter's Charity and will include 12 bouts of boxing that will see an LFB Select team take on a North Kensington team, made-up of men, women and youth boxers from a variety of clubs in the local area and across London.

articles.title: UFC Paris: Kurtis Campbell - from being bullied at school to the UFC
articles.summary: Introduced to combat sports as a seven-year-old after being bullied at school, Kurtis Campbell is now chasing success in the UFC.
articles.body:
Kurtis Campbell was only seven years old when his parents decided something drastically needed to change.

During his time at primary school in Liverpool, Campbell was targeted by bullies. His parents, Jay and Michelle, could see the effect it was having.

It was then that they signed him up for Muay Thai classes to help him learn how to defend himself.

"From there, I've never looked back," Briton Campbell told BBC Sport. "I've been in love with the sport ever since."

Without his parents' influence and support, the 24-year-old would not be chasing his dream of becoming a UFC champion.

Seventeen years later Campbell is preparing for his second fight in the promotion against American Trevor Peek at UFC Paris on Saturday.

"I'm not going to stop until my mum and dad are on a beach somewhere, sipping cocktails and doing nothing else for the rest of their lives," Campbell said.

"They can enjoy it, knowing that they've created this monster. That's my plan."

Initially, it seemed Campbell's time in the gym would serve the sole purpose of learning self-defence before moving to secondary school a couple of years later.

That was until he started competing in amateur competitions, slowly but surely becoming obsessed with his newfound escape from the difficulties he faced at school.

"I was quite a soft kid, in the sense that I didn't really like the violence or the fighting," Campbell said.

"I felt like when I did fight, and when I really did go into it, everything changed and I never looked back."

Aged 15, he won his first international Muay Thai title and started to realise that, with the blessing of his parents, combat sports could become more than just a pastime.

"I was never the cleverest kid. I was always in the bottom sets at school, so I wasn't really focused," Campbell said.

"All of the teachers told me, 'you need to do something else. You have to have a plan B.'"

But for Campbell, who was beginning to attract attention across Merseyside, his unwavering commitment to the sport meant there was no need for a back-up plan.

That included regularly running almost five miles to and from school. There was even one occasion when he missed school while studying for his GCSEs to attend a coaching seminar in Liverpool hosted by John Kavanagh - the coach of former two-weight UFC champion Conor McGregor.

After completing his GCSE exams at the age of 16, Campbell enrolled on a college course that combined studying for a qualification in sport with playing football.

Or at least that was what he was supposed to be doing.

Campbell struck an arrangement with the course leads that allowed him to attend classes before leaving to train in combat sports, while his peers were on the football pitch.

"I was always avoiding anything just for fighting," Campbell said.

"I really didn't like school. It wasn't me. But I made a good few mates there, so you've got to take the pros with the cons."

'That fat kid looking back at me would be proud'

When Campbell suffered a TKO defeat by Danny Silva on his UFC debut in March, it was the first time in almost seven and a half years that he had lost.

Not since December 2018, when he lost to fellow Liverpudlian Liam McCracken on the local amateur circuit, had featherweight Campbell failed to get his hand raised.

He won five titles across three different weight classes with the Full Contact Contender (FCC) promotion before earning a UFC contract on Dana White's Contender Series in September 2025.

It means that when he steps into the Accor Arena to fight Peek, he will face the unfamiliar feeling of trying to bounce back from defeat.

"Fighting in the UFC was just the goal and the dream when I was younger," Campbell said.

"So I feel like that fat kid looking back at me would be proud of me. I would be proud of myself, no matter how the debut went, just because of where I am now.

"I think he'd be happy with me. But I know he'd not be happy with just the story. I've still got a lot of legacy to build.

"That's one thing I would say is good and bad about me - as soon as I get something, I want more of it.

"I don't think I'll ever stop having that feeling."

images.caption: Image caption, Kurtis Campbell won his first contract with the UFC on Dana White's Contender Series last September

articles.title: Andy Ruiz Jr loses comeback fight by unanimous decision but pledges to 'fight again'
articles.summary: Former heavyweight world champion Andy Ruiz Jr fell to a unanimous decision defeat in his first fight in over two years; Anthony Joshua’s former nemesis has struggled with injuries since his success seven years ago
articles.body:
Former heavyweight world champion Ruiz Jr, famous for stripping British boxer Anthony Joshua of his titles seven years ago, took on Poland's Knyba in New Jersey overnight on Friday.

The Mexican fell to a unanimous decision defeat in his first fight in two years, with the judges at the Prudential Center scoring the fight 117-110, 114-113 and 114-113.

Ruiz Jr hit the canvas in the seventh with his legs giving way and had to be saved by the bell, and despite late attempts to knock down Knyba, could not claw the fight back thanks to the Pole's disciplined approach.

The 36-year-old sported a black eye after the bout but Ruiz Jr - who has struggled with injury issues since his rematch defeat to Joshua in 2019 - is not letting the bruising defeat stop his comeback plan.

Ruiz Jr, who recently signed with Eddie Hearn's Matchroom, said: "It was just a long lay-off, and it was a great opponent.

"I didn't want to take an easy fight, so that's why I took Damian. He's a big guy. But we've got to take risks. I've still got it in me, man.

"I've just got to stay active and I want to fight again."

While Ruiz Jr continues to rebuild his career, Knyba will hope to bring himself into the world title mix, calling out German boxer and current WBC heavyweight champion Agit Kabayel after his victory.

"I really want a rematch with Kabayel," he said.

Knyba was knocked out by Kabayel in Germany earlier this year.

articles.title: ONE Fight Night 47: Stamp Fairtex silences her doubts with defiant split-decision win over Selina Flores
articles.summary: Stamp Fairtex secured a split-decision victory in Bangkok; Thai fighter has been returning from serious injury and looks to have returned to her previous form, extending her winning streak to two
articles.body:
For months, she'd questioned whether her body - and more importantly, her mind - was ready. The meniscus tear that ravaged her knee in May 2024 had cast a shadow over every fight since. Hesitation had crept into her performances. Doubt had whispered in her ear.

However at ONE Fight Night 47, which aired live on Sky Sports in the early hours of Saturday morning from Bangkok's Lumpinee Stadium, the Thai megastar silenced those voices with a defiant split-decision victory over two-time WBC Muay Thai world champion Selina 'Teep Queen' Flores, proving she's ready to reclaim what she never stopped believing was hers.

From the opening bell, Stamp was willing to engage. She launched body kicks at Flores, pressured in the clinch, and drove knees upstairs with the precision of a surgeon. The American struggled to find her range at first. Her trademark teeps - the weapons that have made her dangerous - failed to materialise early on.

Flores grew into the second frame. Her low kicks began to find their mark. A sharp right hand cracked cleanly. The signature teep landed, and she finally found her rhythm. But Stamp met fire with fire, her counters arriving with timing that suggests the rust had genuinely fallen away.

The third round reached a crescendo and exploded into chaos. Flores had taken the lead, putting the Thai star on the back foot and often throwing first. Stamp comfortably played the counter game, repeatedly carving her shin into the American's body.

When the American threw a spinning back elbow that sailed past her rival, Stamp didn't hesitate - she flung one back and hit the target. A cartwheel kick followed, drawing roars from the crowd and a nod of respect from her rival. Even the 28-year-old from Pattaya couldn't help but grin from ear to ear.

In the end, the judges split their scorecards - and two of them were swayed by the Thai's output, giving her the win.

It may have been a razor-close victory, but for a fighter who was returning from a serious injury, had dropped a decision in her comeback fight last November, and admitted she had a poor showing in her last victory this past June, it was far more than that.

This was a performance that kept fans on the edge of their seats. The fighter herself was smiling and boldly taking risks on a previously injured leg that made her think twice over the past several months. It was vindication and proof that Stamp Fairtex was truly, finally, back.

Stamp - the first person to hold kickboxing, Muay Thai, and MMA gold in ONE Championship - improved her record to 66-18, and her winning streak extends to two. Whether she pursues the ONE Women's Atomweight MMA world title she relinquished in May 2025 or continues in Muay Thai next, one thing is for certain: she's ready.

Atomweight Muay Thai: Stamp Fairtex defeated Selina Flores via split decision

Featherweight Muay Thai: Ricardo Bravo defeated Mohamed Younes Rabah via knockout at 2:58 of round one

Strawweight MMA: Fabio Henrique defeated Ryohei Kurosawa via unanimous decision

Flyweight Muay Thai: Jordan Estupinan defeated Jaosuayai Mor Krungthepthonburi via unanimous decision

Middleweight Submission Grappling: Pawel Jaworski defeated Rafael Lovato Jr via submission (kneebar) at 1:51 of round one

Featherweight MMA: Pedro Dantas defeated Hector Almonacid via unanimous decision

Atomweight MMA: Macarena Aragon defeated Gabi Fujimoto via submission (scarf-hold Americana) at 2:06 of round three

Strawweight Muay Thai: Elmehdi El Jamari defeated Ngoc Phu Nguyen via TKO at 2:42 of round one

articles.title: Katie Taylor Retirement Fight Odds, Live Stream and KO, Judges' Scorecards Predictions
articles.summary: Women's boxing star Katie Taylor is set to make her final walk to the ring on Saturday when she defends her undipsuted super lightweight title against Flora Pili at Croke Park in Dublin, Ireland.
articles.body:
Women's boxing star Katie Taylor is set to make her final walk to the ring on Saturday when she defends her undipsuted super lightweight title against Flora Pili at Croke Park in Dublin, Ireland.

Taylor's decorated career has included an Olympic gold medal, dominant title reigns and lightweight and super lightweight that included some of the biggest fights in the history of the sport.

Now, she gets the opportunity to close out her career on her terms in her home country against an undefeated contender.

Let's dive in and look at the details you need to catch the fight along with a preview.

Fight Odds, Schedule and Scorecard Prediction

When: Saturday, September 5 at 2 p.m. ET (main event ringwalks at approximately 5:10 p.m.)

Odds: Taylor -3000 ($3,000 bet to win $100); Pili +1320 ($100 bet wins $1,320)

Prediction: Taylor wins via unanimous decision (100-90x2, 99-91)

The stage is set for Taylor to take center stage once more, but this isn't exactly the best opponent she has seen. Pili is undefeated in 12 professional fights, but the quality of competition is reflected in the odds.

The Frenchwoman most recently claimed the IBO title with a majority decision over Jelena Janićijević. It was good enough to set her up with this opportunity. It just wasn't good enough to make her a viable threat.

Still, Taylor isn't overlooking her opponent as she looks to add one more statement victory to her resume.

"People have travelled all around the world to follow my career and I'm hoping I can repay some of that with a big performance on September 5," she told Matchroom Boxing . "I'm under no illusions that Flora will present a very tough challenge, she's undefeated as a professional and has a good amateur pedigree so I have the utmost respect for her."

Taylor, 40, is 11 years older than her opponent on Saturday night. However, she still should hold the advantage in hand speed, athleticism and talent.

Pili is a skilled boxer, but she doesn't pose much threat in the power department. She has finished just two of her 12 career wins. Taylor has been drawn into some fire fights in the later part of her career, but that shouldn't be a problem on Saturday.

The Croke Park crowd should get exactly what they are hoping for: A one-sided affair where the native daughter showcases her skills one last time.

articles.title: Katie Taylor vs. Flora Pili Live Updates and Highlights From Tonight's Card
articles.summary: Who says you can't go home?
articles.body:
Like the Ruiz fight card in New Jersey on Friday, the Taylor show in Ireland presents multiple opportunities for those interested in cashing in on upset hunches.

Taylor is a -2000 favorite according to lines set by DraftKings, and a $100 flyer on Pili, who's unbeaten in 12 pro fights, would yield a $1,000 profit.

Not only did Ruiz lose on Friday night, but so did -700 favorite Alan Chaves earlier on the card.

Elsewhere on Saturday's show, heavyweight Dave Allen, who's been KO'd five times in nine career losses, is a -245 proposition to beat +190 underdog Thomas Carty, and Tyrone McKenna and Emmet Brennan are +900 and +300 underdogs, respectively, in their main-card matches with Paddy Donovan and Taylor Bevan.

articles.title: UFC Paris live updates: Dan Hooker vs. Salahdine Parnasse round-by-round coverage
articles.summary: Follow along for live updates and round-by-round scoring for UFC Fight Night 287 in Paris.
articles.body:
PARIS – UFC Fight Night 287 takes place Saturday, and you can join us for live round-by-round coverage and official results from the card beginning at noon ET (9 a.m. PT).

The 14-fight card goes down at Accor Arena in France and streams entirely on Paramount+ .

In the main event, longtime UFC lightweight Dan Hooker (24-14 MMA, 14-10 UFC) will try to spoil the promotional debut of French star Salahdine Parnasse (23-2 MMA, 0-0 UFC), who is a heavy betting favorite in front of his home fans.

Additionally, it's France vs. France in the lightweight co-feature when Axel Sola (12-1-1 MMA, 2-1 UFC) takes on Fares Ziam (18-5 MMA, 8-3 UFC). Plus, Michael Page (25-3 MMA, 4-1 UFC) returns to middleweight for a clash with Nursulton Ruziboev (37-9-2 MMA, 5-1 UFC).

Follow along with our round-by-round updates and official results beginning at noon ET for the preliminary card and 3 p.m. ET for the main card on the Paramount+ streaming platform.

articles.body:
Next up, we'll head to the heavyweight division. In one corner, we'll have Portuguese giant Mario Pinto (12-0). In the other, we'll have Ryan Spann (24-11), who made the trip to Paris from Texas.

Pinto is one of several exciting new arrivals in the UFC heavyweight division, and is now 3-0 in the promotion, most recently beating Felipe Franco by decision.

Spann, a former light heavyweight, has seemingly found new life at heavyweight, having most recently choked out Lukasz Brzeski and knocked out BJJ legend Marcus "Buchecha" Almeida.

Both guys are very tall, and very powerful. Don't blink in this one.

articles.standfirst: 'El Potro Menorquín' se estrena con victoria por decisión unánime en la mejor liga de MMA del mundo
articles.summary: 'El Potro Menorquín' se estrena con victoria por decisión unánime en la mejor liga de MMA del mundo
articles.body: Entrar por la puerta grande. Fabià Sintes (12-3) silenció el Accor Arena de París derrotando por decisión unánime al local Michael Aljarouj (13-4) en su estreno en UFC. 'El Potro Menorquín' controló los dos últimos asaltos y dejó una 'masterclass' de como controlar el combate en la lucha y en el suelo. Era el 'game plan'... y funcionó. Tras un primer asalto muy igualado en el que Aljarouj defendió bien los derribos del que fuera campeón del peso mosca de WOW... Sintes se impuso. Fabià encontró la forma de llevar a Aljarouj al suelo y lo destruyó en el segundo 'round' a base de codazos una vez lograda la posición en la montada. Aljarouj, pese a un arrebato de orgullo y carácter en el último minuto del combate, se desfondó y sucumbió ante la polivalencia y verstalidad de un Fabià que entra de la mejor forma posible en la mejor liga de MMA del mundo. Victoria fuera de casa, en Francia y ante un francés, para dejar su impronta y confirmar que se ha ganado de sobra su contrato con UFC.

images.caption: Fabià Sintes celebra su triunfo en UFC. UFC París.

articles.title: UFC Paris live results, highlights and play-by-play
articles.summary: UFC Paris results, highlights, live discussion and instant play-by-play, reactions and analysis.
articles.body:
Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) is live THIS AFTERNOON (Sat., Sept. 5, 2026) with UFC Paris , streaming live online via Paramount+ . The event happens at Accor Arena in Paris, France, featuring a special Octagon newcomer in the main event.

Salahdine Parnasse vs. Dan Hooker is our main event, going down in the Lightweight division. Parnasse is a long-time former KSW champion who made a big splash with his one and done appearance at MVP MMA . The reason he was done there was because UFC wanted to poach him out of that fledgling promotion before he drew too many serious mixed martial arts (MMA) fans over to it. Hooker comes into this one off two losses and looking very much like a sacrificial lamb. However, as last week taught us, -600 odds can be overcome .

The co-main is an all French affair, in the Featherweight division, with Fares Ziam meeting Axel Sola . Both of these guys are action fighters known for putting on a show. They should get the crowd roaring in Paris, even if it's not obvious to the locals whom they should be cheering for.

Rounding out the main card is Michael Page vs. Nursulton Ruziboev , Daniil Donchenko vs. Punahele Soriano , Kurtis Campbell vs. Trevor Peek and Losene Keita vs. Muhammad Naimov . Page might be trying to fight out of his UFC contract here, which is the reason UFC has pared him with a big, rangy striker who can also make you quit on the ground.

The featured "Prelim" is Morgan Charriere vs. Felipe Lima . The undercard also boasts Mario Pinto vs. Ryan Spann , Oumar Sy vs. Modestas Bukauskas and Nathaniel Wood against late replacement Pavel Andrusca . Further down the card we have Michael Aljarouj vs. Fabia Sintes , Nora Cornolle vs. Klaudia Sygula , Matthieu Duclos vs. Lucas Felipe Dias and Delphine Benouaich vs. Sofia Montenegro to make up the numbers. Aljarouj does look like an intriguing prospect, though.

We are operating at prime local time today. That means it is an extremely early wake up for me and anyone else on the east coast. Checkout these special air times below:

UFC Paris "Prelims" will begin at 12 p.m. ET .

UFC Paris main card is scheduled to start at 3 p.m. ET .

All of UFC Paris airs on Paramount+ , which you can stream here .

The live blog here starts rolling below at 12 p.m. ET . Come in and say hi!

155 lbs.: Salahdine Parnasse vs. Dan Hooker

185 lbs.: Michael Page vs. Nursulton Ruziboev

145 lbs.: Kurtis Campbell vs. Trevor Peek

170 lbs.: Daniil Donchenko vs. Punahele Soriano

145 lbs.: Losene Keita vs. Muhammad Naimov

145 lbs.: Morgan Charriere vs. Felipe Lima

205 lbs.: Modestas Bukauskas def. Oumar Sy by TKO (punches), round 2 (3:57)

145 lbs.: Pavel Andrusca def. Nathaniel Wood by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 29-28)

125 lbs.: Fabia Sintes def. Michael Alarouj by unanimous decision (29-28, 29-28, 29-27)

135 lbs.: Nora Cornolle def. Klaudia Sygula by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 30-27)

185 lbs.: Matthieu Duclos def. Luis Felipe Dias by TKO (check hook), round 1 (4:45) — HIGHLIGHTS

115 lbs.: Delphine Benouiach def. Sofia Montenegro by technical submission (rear naked choke), round 2 (4:22) — HIGHLIGHTS

Oumar Sy vs. Modestas Bukauskas: What a comeback? Sy dominated Bukauskas in the first round, pinning him down and coming close to a ground and pound finish. Bukauskas got up, though, at the urging of the referee and was able to survive. Turns out all that domination tired out Sy. In the second Bukauskas was able to get up quickly from a Sy takedown and then he turned up the pace, putting a beating on Sy on the feet. The tired Sy crumbled and Bakauskas was able to come away with a real gutsy win over Sy (whose time as a top prospect seems to be over).

Official decision: Modestas Bukauskas def. Oumar Sy by TKO (punches), round 2 (3:57)

Nathaniel Wood vs. Pavel Andrusca : Wood looked good early on, stinging Andrusca with his striking. At that point Andrusca, a late replacement making his debut looked a little out of his depth. That might have just been Octagon jitters, though. As the fight went on he looked more comfortable and his wrestling started to give Wood a lot of problems. Andrusca was able to take Wood down and threaten with a submission in the second and then start beating him to the punch in the third. I scored it 29-28 for the newcomer.

Official decision: Pavel Andrusca def. Nathaniel Wood by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 29-28)

Michael Alarouj vs. Fabia Sintes: Alarouj's striking looked nice in the first round, but his inability to stop a naked single leg takedown meant he spent far more of this fight on his back than he would have liked to. After a close opening round spent mainly on the feet, Sintes was able to suck up lots of control time in the second and third. Alarouj mounted a comeback in the third, but was unable to do any serious damage. I scored the fight for Sintes, to break France's winning streak.

Official decision: Fabia Sintes def. Michael Alarouj by unanimous decision (29-28, 29-28, 29-27)

Nora Cornolle vs. Klaudia Sygula: The clinch was the story of this fight. Cornolle, the bigger body, was able to establish the clinch often in this fight and prevent Sygula from gaining an advantage through her better speed and volume striking. It wasn't pretty, but Cornolle did a good job of bullying Sygula around and getting a convincing decision.

Official decision: Nora Cornolle def. Klaudia Sygula by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 30-27)

Matthieu Duclos vs. Luis Felipe Dias: Another brawl! Dias might have been winning this one, landing plenty on Duclos as he blitzed forwards. He was very wild, though. Eventually he ran into a check hook and was briefly knocked out. He seemed to wake up when he hit the ground and was defending himself as the referee came in to break it up.

Official decision: Matthieu Duclos def. Luis Felipe Dias by TKO (check hook), round 1 (4:45)

Delphine Benouaich vs. Sofia Montenegro: that was a brutal start to the event. Benouaich and Montenegro throw down from the opening bell. Benouiach landed the cleaner shots early, but Montenegro's offense seemed to be wearing on her more. In the second, though, she landed a hard straight punch right to the jaw. That put down Montengro and Benouiach then split her open with brutal elbows. With Montenegro bleeding all over the place, Benouiach then took the back and choked her to sleep. Keep an eye on this girl!

Official decision: Delphine Benouiach def. Sofia Montenegro by technical submission (rear naked choke), round 2 (4:22)

articles.title: Katie Taylor vs. Flora Pili live results, round-by-round updates, ring walks for today's retirement fight
articles.summary: Follow Katie Taylor vs. Flora Pili live results and round-by-round updates for the Taylor vs. Pili fight card on Saturday at Croke Park. Taylor, perhaps the women's boxing GOAT, will retire after tonight's bout.
articles.body: Uncrowned has Katie Taylor vs. Flora Pili live results, round-by-round updates, ring walks, highlights and start time for the Taylor vs. Pili fight card on Saturday at Croke Park in Dublin, Ireland. Irish boxing legend Katie Taylor fights for the final time in her storied career against Flora Pili, with the undisputed super lightweight title on the line.Taylor (25-1, 6 KOs), Uncrowned's No. 2 pound-for-pound boxer, is a two-weight undisputed champion. She became the undisputed super lightweight champion with a majority decision victory over Chantelle Cameron in their November 2023 rematch.Taylor has earned two more wins over Amanda Serrano since that fight, but had to drop her WBC title after the Serrano trilogy. The Irishwoman will look to reclaim that belt on Saturday in front of 80,000 fans at Croke Park and leave boxing as an undisputed champion.Pili (12-0, 2 KOs) is the reigning IBO champion and also Taylor's mandatory challenger for her IBF crown. Pili recorded a career-best win last December, defeating Serbia's Jelena Janićijević by majority decision.The Taylor vs. Pili prelims begin at 11 a.m. ET and can be watched below on Uncrowned.The main card starts at 2 p.m. ET on DAZN, with main event ring walks expected around 5 p.m. ETFollow all of the action with Uncrowned's live results and play-by-play of the main card below.Main card (2 p.m. ET, DAZN)WBA, WBC, IBF and WBO Super Lightweight titles: Katie Taylor vs. Flora PiliHeavyweight: David Allen vs. Thomas CartyWelterweight: Paddy Donovan vs. Tyrone McKennaSuper middleweight: Taylor Bevan vs. Emmet BrennanPrelims (11 a.m. ET, Watch on Uncrowned)Bantamweight: Molly McCann def.
